tasks.short: Notify responsible parties of confirmed breaches, required remedies and possible consequences.

steps.what: Retrieve approved findings, recipient details and applicable obligations.
Determine appropriate warning, remedy, deadline and escalation within delegated authority.
Prepare warning using findings, approved wording and notice instructions.
Approve wording, proportionality, recipient and authority to issue the warning.
Explain the approved warning, required remedies and available response channels.
Record delivery, response and remedy deadlines in the case record.

tasks.design: Configure the {WORKFLOW} to assemble approved findings and generate notices from controlled templates in the {DOCS}. Approval unlocks the specific notice and recipient; the compliance officer handles the conversation. A short structured response form creates the case record and schedules remedy reminders in the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence, templates and delivery records were separated. Consequences often depended on judgement and delegated authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and template features handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting evidence and deadline records.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, proportionality and sensitive conversations remain difficult. A company compliance officer usually cannot impose public-law penalties.
tasks.human_edge: Explain consequences fairly, recognise contested facts and distinguish a warning from a threat beyond company authority.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly triage of overdue high-risk remedies

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling notices and chasing dates. The officer can propose remedy escalations twice weekly; sanction and enforcement rights do not expand.

reach.task: Prioritise overdue remedies by financial exposure.
reach.learn: Exposure estimation, risk appetite and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Controlled templates, approval routing and reminders can automate warning administration; these time shares are estimates.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment when solely automated decisions significantly affect a natural person.

assumptions: The officer communicates company compliance findings within delegated authority.
Approved notice templates cover routine warnings; unusual wording stays with a person.
The approval in s4 supplies the action gate in s5.
The split retains substantial judgement and conversation time despite the automation prior.
Build ranges are estimates in working days and include national consultation where applicable; formal procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Who may approve warnings, contractual consequences and regulator referrals?
What proportion of warnings requires a live conversation?
Are recipient details, delivery evidence and deadlines available through supported interfaces?
Which national consultation requirements apply to case tracking?
research_questions: Which warnings can use fixed wording without weakening explanation or response rights?
What delivery evidence is required for each notice category?
new_work: Maintain notice templates and delegated-authority limits.
Review delivery failures and incorrect recipient details.
Confirm structured response records after sensitive conversations.
Handle disputed notices and overdue remedies.
tasks.statement: Warn violators of infractions or penalties.

tasks.short: Review applications and supporting records for eligibility, obligations and potential liability.

steps.what: Receive the application and register its supporting documents.
Check identifiers, dates and financial records against required fields.
Read supporting documents and extract facts relevant to eligibility or liability.

loop.input: Case documents and a fixed list of required facts.
loop.output: Typed facts with document references, exact supporting passages and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate field types and source locations; a person verifies material facts and contradictions.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting evidence goes to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative documents express relevant facts in varied wording; field mappings handle only structured submissions.

steps.what: Assess eligibility or liability and identify unresolved questions.
Request missing evidence from the applicant or responsible party.
Finalise findings or record that the assessment awaits further evidence.

tasks.design: A case register in the {WORKFLOW} links submissions in the {DOCS} to deterministic checks on the {ERP}. A bounded extraction loop creates a source-linked evidence pack; the officer assesses contested facts and approves findings. Missing-evidence requests use fixed templates in the {EMAIL}, with approval before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supporting documents varied, evidence was scattered and exceptions did not fit simple eligibility rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured validation is established technology. Bounded document extraction and cheaper integration development make the remaining preparation work more practical.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity, conflicting evidence and legal interpretation remain difficult. A complete dossier does not establish eligibility by itself.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh contradictory evidence, interpret obligations and recognise when specialist legal advice is needed.

ambition.what: Permit-readiness preflight for proposed operational projects

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching documents to reviewing evidence and advising project owners before submission. The officer can recommend readiness; authority to grant permits or determine legal liability does not change.

reach.task: Validate financial evidence used in eligibility assessments.
reach.learn: Ledger provenance, reconciliations and materiality.

evidence.claim: Veeva RIM tracks registrations and submissions, supporting the feasibility of controlled regulatory dossier management.
Source-linked extraction can reduce evidence preparation, but the digest supplies no measured eligibility-review outcome.
A determining score can engage GDPR automated-decision protections; advisory labels alone do not settle the issue.

assumptions: The company reviews its own obligations or counterparties rather than exercising public licensing powers.
Incomplete cases repeat evidence collection and assessment before final findings.
The document-heavy prior supports extraction, but low rule coverage keeps substantive assessment human.
GDPR and the EU AI Act require use-specific assessment; national consultation may apply.
Build ranges include access and applicable consultation in working days; statutory procedures can extend the calendar.
unknowns: Which eligibility criteria are explicit, versioned and approved?
Which documents contain personal or special-category data?
What authority does the officer have to finalise findings?
How often are documents unreadable, contradictory or suspected to be false?
Are supported interfaces available for financial records and case files?
research_questions: Which facts can be validated against authoritative records?
What evidence omissions could materially change an assessment?
Does the proposed processing require a DPIA or fall within an EU AI Act high-risk use?
new_work: Verify material extracted facts and source passages.
Resolve conflicting or unreadable documents.
Maintain required fields and versioned assessment criteria.
Monitor extraction errors, permissions and retention.
Retest document handling when submission formats change.
tasks.statement: Evaluate applications, records, or documents to gather information about eligibility or liability issues.

tasks.short: Advise employees and counterparties on licence and permit requirements within the company's remit.

steps.what: Receive the question and identify the activity, jurisdiction and deadline.
Find current obligations and approved guidance for the stated activity and jurisdiction.
Clarify missing facts and the practical decision the requester needs to make.
Draft an explanation of requirements, next actions and unresolved issues.

loop.input: Clarified request and current approved guidance selected by jurisdiction and activity.
loop.output: Draft advice with source passages, next actions and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Reject unsupported citations and expired guidance; the officer checks applicability and material claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per request; absent or conflicting guidance routes to specialist review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Case-specific explanations require combining facts with varied guidance; fixed answers cover only routine questions.

steps.what: Approve the interpretation or refer unresolved legal questions to legal counsel.
Explain the approved advice and answer questions about practical next steps.
Log advice, sources and agreed follow-up actions.

tasks.design: An intake form in the {WORKFLOW} selects current guidance in the {DOCS} by activity and jurisdiction. Fixed answers cover routine questions, while a bounded loop drafts explanations for more varied requests. The officer approves case-specific advice, handles the conversation and confirms the resulting advice record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance lacked reliable jurisdiction and version tags. Questions often arrived without enough facts to choose an answer.
tasks.enabler_now: A controlled guidance index supports deterministic retrieval. Bounded drafting can turn selected guidance into clearer explanations without searching beyond approved sources.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability, regulatory change and implied reliance on advice remain difficult. Maintaining the guidance library takes continuing expert time.
tasks.human_edge: Discover the real business question, explain uncertainty and recognise when advice exceeds delegated expertise.

ambition.what: Permit guidance sessions for frontline purchasing coordinators

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time searching and drafting, and more time on practical guidance and difficult interpretations. They can offer sessions to purchasing coordinators; legal interpretation rights remain subject to existing delegation.

reach.task: Assess the cash and timing impact of permit requirements.
reach.learn: Cash-flow dependencies, project commitments and funding approval.

evidence.claim: Controlled retrieval and bounded drafting are feasible patterns; the digest contains no direct licensing-advice deployment.
A documented report failure involved nonexistent sources, supporting explicit citation checks before advice is used.

assumptions: The typical corporate remit concerns business licences and permits; passport determinations belong to competent authorities.
Approved guidance has jurisdiction, effective-date and owner metadata.
Routine requests may skip clarification or a live explanation; the shares represent a mixed caseload.
The approval in s5 supplies the action gate in s6; unresolved legal questions require counsel clearance.
GDPR applies to request records; national consultation requirements depend on the implementation.
Build estimates include guidance setup, access and applicable consultation in working days.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions and licence categories are in scope?
Who approves guidance updates and difficult interpretations?
How frequently do requesters need live explanations?
Which requesters may access each guidance category?
Does an approved, current guidance library already exist?
research_questions: Which recurring questions can be answered safely with fixed approved text?
How will source changes invalidate earlier guidance and open advice drafts?
Which facts must be collected before advice can be applicable?
new_work: Maintain guidance versions, jurisdiction tags and access permissions.
Review draft applicability and supporting sources.
Route novel questions to legal counsel.
Confirm follow-up actions and correct advice records.
Turn recurring resolved questions into approved fixed answers.
tasks.statement: Advise licensees or other individuals or groups concerning licensing, permit, or passport regulations.

tasks.short: Prepare compliance reports with verified evidence, evaluations, recommendations and decisions.

steps.what: Collect case records, approved findings, advice records and financial evidence.
Reconcile case totals, dates and financial amounts in a reporting workbook.
Evaluate significant findings and agree recommendations with control owners.
Write the report with evidence, metrics, conclusions and recommendations.

loop.input: Validated metrics, approved findings, human conclusions and a controlled report template.
loop.output: Report narrative linked to evidence; deterministic tables retain their validated values.
loop.check: Compare all figures with validated metrics, verify source references and check that conclusions match approved inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per report; unsupported statements are removed or returned to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and fixed sections are deterministic, but a readable synthesis of varied findings needs bounded drafting.

steps.what: Approve conclusions, recommendations, disclosures and the intended audience.
Send the approved report to authorised recipients.
Archive the approved report, evidence references and distribution record.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collect controlled records from the {WORKFLOW}, {ERP} and {DOCS}, reconcile metrics and feed the {BI}. A report generator inserts validated tables and uses a bounded loop for narrative based on human conclusions. Approval in the {WORKFLOW} releases the exact report to its authorised audience through the {EMAIL} and archives its evidence in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports required repeated collection and workbook reconciliation. Recommendations depended on context that was poorly captured in source records.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic joins, reconciliations and templates are established. AI-assisted coding lowers assembly effort, while bounded drafting can work from approved conclusions.
tasks.still_hard: Data definitions, evidence completeness and materiality remain expensive to resolve. Narrative can overstate what the evidence establishes.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a technical exception from a material compliance failure and recommend a proportionate response.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of remediation funding requests

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time assembling periodic reports and can bring current evidence to weekly funding discussions. They gain a stronger recommendation role; budget approval remains with the financial manager.

reach.task: Build reliable compliance trend measures.
reach.learn: Metric definitions, data lineage and reconciliation controls.

reach.task: Compare remediation funding requests.
reach.learn: Cost-benefit assessment, financial exposure and budget constraints.

evidence.claim: Records, reconciliations, dashboards and report tables are suitable for deterministic automation; estimates are not measured outcomes.
Veeva RIM supports controlled regulatory submissions, an adjacent capability rather than proof of general compliance-report automation.
A documented government-report failure included nonexistent sources, supporting evidence checks before report release.

assumptions: The reporting workbook currently bridges case and financial records; some companies already perform these checks in the {BI}.
Report conclusions are supplied by people rather than inferred as binding decisions by the drafting loop.
The approval in s5 supplies the release gate in s6, including approval of any external recipients.
The report-writing prior supports drafting automation, but evaluation and recommendation work remain substantial.
GDPR governs personal data in reports; access, retention and national consultation requirements are assessed during setup.
Build ranges are working-day estimates and include applicable consultation; formal approval timelines may extend them.
unknowns: Which reports are internal, contractual or regulatory?
Are metrics defined consistently across source systems?
Which recipients and disclosures require additional approval?
What retention, evidence and submission requirements apply?
Do reports include employee-level monitoring or sensitive case details?
research_questions: Which report sections can be generated entirely from structured records?
How should corrected source records affect previously approved reports?
What reconciliation tolerances are appropriate for each financial measure?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions before report generation.
Review narrative against evidence and approved conclusions.
Maintain metric definitions, templates and recipient permissions.
Monitor failed extracts, delivery failures and archive completeness.
Retest connectors when source schemas change.
tasks.statement: Prepare reports of activities, evaluations, recommendations, or decisions.

tasks.short: Assess suspected violations and report them to the appropriate authority.

steps.what: Assemble incident records and supporting evidence from the {DOCS}.
Compare evidence with applicable obligations and record possible breaches.

loop.input: Evidence bundle and approved, versioned obligations for the relevant jurisdiction.
loop.output: Possible breaches, contrary evidence, uncertainties and source references.
loop.check: Require valid source references; the officer checks applicability and factual support.
loop.stop: One assessment and one correction pass; unresolved questions return to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative evidence and contextual obligations cannot all be compared through fixed fields.

steps.what: Decide reporting duty, recipient, deadline and information scope.
Draft the violation report and identify its supporting attachments.

loop.input: Reporting decision, approved template and referenced evidence.
loop.output: Draft report with evidence references and explicit missing information.
loop.check: Validate required fields and references; the officer checks claims and disclosure scope.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported statements remain flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: The factual narrative varies by incident; fixed fields alone cannot express it.

steps.what: Review the report and authorise its disclosure.
Submit the approved report through the {GOV_PORTAL}.
File the submission receipt and update the case status in the {WORKFLOW}.

tasks.design: A case flow in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves authorised evidence from the {DOCS}, checks deadlines and runs bounded assessment and drafting loops. The officer decides reportability, and an authorised signatory approves the exact disclosure before a deterministic connector submits it through the {GOV_PORTAL} and records the receipt.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is scattered, obligations require interpretation, and submission channels differ. Templates alone do not assemble a defensible report.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case flows and document access can support deterministic collection and deadline checks. Bounded drafting can reduce narrative work when every claim retains its source.
tasks.still_hard: Reporting thresholds, privilege, conflicting obligations and urgent deadlines remain difficult. Some authorities offer no supported submission interface.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising material facts, resolving legal ambiguity and accepting responsibility for disclosure.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of incidents approaching a reporting deadline.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time assembling and filing reports and more time assessing evidence and urgent cases. Legal reporting and disclosure authority remain with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Prepare a traceable evidence pack for a control failure.
reach.learn: Evidence provenance, control testing and reconciliation to source records.

reach.task: Prioritise incidents by potential financial exposure.
reach.learn: Exposure estimation, uncertainty ranges and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Case assembly, deadline checks and receipt logging can use deterministic workflows; these are design estimates.
Veeva RIM tracks registrations and publishes submissions in a specialised regulatory setting; this is adjacent capability evidence.
The documented flawed-report case supports checking generated claims against their original sources.

assumptions: The company has a compliance function and reports violations relevant to its activities.
Step shares are illustrative, not measured. Evidence assessment and approval remain substantial despite the workflow-automation prior.
Automatic submission requires a supported interface and an approval bound to the exact report, attachments and recipient.
Build ranges cover one reporting route and are working-day estimates, not elapsed delivery promises.
GDPR applies to personal evidence; EU AI Act applicability depends on intended use. Access work includes national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Applicable reporting regimes, recipients and deadlines.
Who may approve disclosure and whether urgent cases have a delegated route.
Supported submission interfaces and authentication methods.
Evidence sensitivity, retention periods and privilege restrictions.
Whether employee-data processing triggers consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which reporting routes support reliable submission acknowledgements and duplicate prevention?
Which report sections can use fixed fields without a drafting loop?
new_work: Review cited assessments and generated report narratives.
Maintain obligation versions, recipient mappings and deadline rules.
Handle unavailable submission channels and uncertain delivery.
Audit approval records, access permissions and disclosure scope.
tasks.statement: Report law or regulation violations to appropriate boards or agencies.

tasks.short: Interview applicants and specialists to clarify facts relevant to licensing decisions.

steps.what: Read the application file and prepare questions about missing or conflicting facts.

loop.input: Application file and approved licensing standards.
loop.output: Source-linked evidence gaps, contradictions and suggested neutral questions.
loop.check: Validate source references; the officer checks relevance and removes unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: One brief and one correction pass; unresolved gaps remain questions for the interview.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative applications can contain inconsistencies that required-field checks cannot identify.

steps.what: Arrange the interview and request outstanding documents through the {EMAIL}.
Interview the applicant or specialist and probe relevant uncertainties.
Write a factual interview summary and list unresolved questions.

loop.input: Officer's interview notes and supplied evidence.
loop.output: Attributed factual summary separating statements, documents and unresolved questions.
loop.check: The officer verifies attribution, omissions and references against the original notes.
loop.stop: One summary and one revision; ambiguous passages return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes require synthesis; fixed forms cannot reliably preserve their meaning.

steps.what: Clarify disputed technical facts through the {EMAIL}.
Attach the reviewed summary and clarification to the application file.

tasks.design: A case flow in the {WORKFLOW} prepares a source-linked interview brief from the {DOCS} and arranges appointments through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. The officer conducts the interview, reviews a bounded summary drafted from their notes, and files the reviewed record for the licensing decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main work is a contextual conversation. Preparation and note writing depend on varied application documents that simple scheduling tools cannot interpret.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling and filing can use existing configuration. Small document-reading and drafting loops can prepare questions and summaries without replacing the interview.
tasks.still_hard: Building trust, probing evasive answers, accommodating communication needs and resolving specialist disagreement.
tasks.human_edge: Asking fair follow-up questions and understanding explanations in context without treating demeanour as proof.

ambition.what: An applicant-facing evidence-gap checklist before the interview.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends more of the week on substantive interviews and difficult factual questions. No licensing decision rights change.

reach.task: Prepare a neutral chronology for a fact-finding interview.
reach.learn: Non-leading questions, evidence attribution and separating inconsistency from deception.

reach.task: Request specialist evidence needed to resolve an eligibility question.
reach.learn: Scope precise evidence requests and document the limits of specialist conclusions.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, document requests and filing can be configured; interview preparation and summaries can use bounded model loops.
Workplace emotion recognition is prohibited under the EU AI Act; it is excluded from this design.

assumptions: Licensing interviews apply only where the company operates an authorised licensing or certification service.
Step shares are illustrative. Conversation remains the largest share, consistent with the supplied means prior.
The design uses officer-written notes and introduces no recording, emotion analysis or applicant scoring.
Scheduling messages use approved templates and minimum necessary case details.
The evidence-gap checklist requires officer review before applicant delivery.
GDPR applies to application records. Access estimates include national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Whether this licensing activity exists in the company.
Interview participants, languages and accessibility needs.
Which documents may be shared with external specialists.
Required opportunities for applicants to correct factual records.
Case volumes, interview duration and retention requirements.
research_questions: Which common evidence gaps can be detected using form validation alone?
What summary format best preserves attribution and unresolved disagreement?
new_work: Review suggested questions and applicant-facing evidence requests.
Check summaries for omissions, attribution errors and unsupported conclusions.
Maintain interview templates and document-access rules.
Handle scheduling exceptions and accessible participation requests.
tasks.statement: Confer with or interview officials, technical or professional specialists, or applicants to obtain information or to clarify facts relevant to licensing decisions.

tasks.short: Review eligibility and issue licences within an authorised licensing mandate.

steps.what: Register the application in the {OTHER} licensing register.
Check qualifications and supporting documents against the application.

loop.input: Application documents and required evidence fields.
loop.output: Evidence fields with page references, missing items and conflicting details.
loop.check: Validate field formats and dates; the officer verifies material facts and authenticity separately.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry for failed fields; uncertain items enter manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supporting documents vary in layout and wording; structured submissions bypass the loop.

steps.what: Complete the standards checklist, including payment status where required.
Decide eligibility, conditions and permitted validity period.
Prepare the licence certificate from the approved decision.
Send the authorised licence certificate to the applicant through the {EMAIL}.
Record licence status and expiry in the {OTHER} licensing register.

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} licensing register for structured intake and completeness checks, with a bounded extraction loop for documents in the {DOCS}. Deterministic rules prepare the eligibility checklist; the licensing officer authorises the decision, after which a generator creates the certificate and the {WORKFLOW} sends it through the {EMAIL} and updates the register.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence arrives in varied documents, standards contain discretionary elements, and certificate preparation is separated from the eligibility record.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake, versioned rules and template generation already support much of the work. Bounded extraction can handle document variation without making the licensing decision.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity checks, recognition of equivalent qualifications, discretionary conditions and appeals. Integration cannot create a legal power to issue licences.
tasks.human_edge: Applying standards fairly to unusual evidence and giving a defensible reason for conditions or refusal.
tasks.altitude: The officer reviews eligibility and exceptional evidence instead of rekeying documents and producing certificates. Statutory powers and delegated decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess whether evidence satisfies a defined authorisation requirement.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, qualification equivalence and reasoned decision records.

reach.task: Analyse application delays by evidence gap and review stage.
reach.learn: Event definitions, cohort analysis and avoiding misleading averages.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, versioned eligibility rules and certificate templates can automate administration while retaining human decisions.
Veeva RIM supports registration records and regulatory submissions; it does not establish this individual-licensing use case.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its exceptions and safeguards.

assumptions: Most mid-size companies apply for licences rather than issue them. This task applies only to an authorised issuer or delegated operator.
The scenario covers one licence family and an existing licensing register that supports configuration.
Step shares are illustrative. Clear rule coverage supports automated checks, but those checks are not the final decision.
The updated application file includes any required interview record; a complete initial file can serve the same purpose.
Issuance authorisation specifies identity, licence type, conditions and validity. Generated certificates must match it exactly before release.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; national rules determine licensing powers, procedure and consultation requirements.
unknowns: Whether the company has any licence-issuing mandate.
Which standards are objective and which require discretion.
Required identity, authenticity and qualification checks.
Signature, certificate-format and delivery requirements.
Payment prerequisites, appeal rights and publication obligations.
Existing register interfaces and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which licence fields and checks can be configured in the existing register?
Which decisions require a legally designated officer or an additional signatory?
How will the release process prevent duplicate or unauthorised certificates?
new_work: Verify extracted evidence and investigate authenticity concerns.
Maintain versioned standards, fee prerequisites and certificate templates.
Test changes against borderline and historical cases.
Handle delivery failures, corrections, revocations and appeals.
Review access logs and decision traceability.
tasks.statement: Issue licenses to individuals meeting standards.

tasks.short: Assess licence fees, collect payments and resolve payment exceptions.

steps.what: Determine the licence fee and any applicable exemption in the {ERP}.
Issue the fee invoice and payment instructions from the {ERP}.
Match imported {BANK} transactions to fee invoices in the {ERP}.
Investigate unmatched payments and disputed fees through the {EMAIL}.
Approve fee adjustments or refunds within delegated limits in the {ERP}.
Send payment reminders through the {EMAIL} for undisputed overdue invoices.
Update payment status in the {OTHER} licensing register.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to calculate published fees, issue invoices with unique references and send scheduled reminders through the {EMAIL}. A deterministic connector matches imported {BANK} transactions and synchronises payment status with the {OTHER} licensing register; staff investigate exceptions and a finance manager approves adjustments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment references and application identifiers do not consistently align across the licensing register and the {ERP}. Responsibility crosses licensing and finance teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing invoicing and reconciliation features can handle routine cases once identifiers and fee rules are aligned. A small connector can replace repeated payment-status checks.
tasks.still_hard: Third-party payers, partial payments, disputed exemptions and refunds. Fee changes and settlement timing must remain consistent across records.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving disputed charges fairly and distinguishing payment mistakes from genuine entitlement to an adjustment.
tasks.altitude: The officer stops checking routine receipts and works mainly on disputed fees and licensing prerequisites. Finance retains adjustment and payment authority; no new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Maintain accurate invoice references and fee categories.
reach.learn: Receivables controls, exemption evidence and invoice correction procedures.

reach.task: Reconcile licence receipts to open invoices.
reach.learn: Partial-payment handling, duplicate detection and settlement reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Published fee rules, invoicing, reference matching and reminders are primarily deterministic finance operations.
Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates; this supports the narrower principle of rule-based amount checking, not licence-fee collection.

assumptions: This task applies only where the company legitimately charges licence or certification fees.
Published fees and standard exemptions can be represented as approved rules.
The {ERP} supports invoicing, imported bank transactions and approval configuration.
Step shares are illustrative. The structured payment steps support more automation than the supplied human-task prior suggests.
Ambiguous matches remain unmatched; the design uses no model loop and makes no automatic withdrawal from applicants.
Refund execution remains in the existing treasury process after approval; it is outside this fee-collection task.
GDPR applies to payer data. Access estimates include segregation of duties and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Whether licence fees are charged and who legally sets them.
Fee schedules, tax treatment and exemption rules.
Payment channels, reference quality and reconciliation volumes.
Bank-feed availability and register integration support.
Refund authority, approval limits and existing treasury controls.
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} matching rules resolve routine receipts without custom matching code?
Which settlement events are sufficient to mark an application paid?
How should disputed invoices suppress reminders across both records?
new_work: Maintain fee schedules, exemption rules and application-reference mappings.
Investigate unmatched, duplicate and partial payments.
Monitor import failures and reconciliation totals.
Review adjustment requests and route approved refunds to treasury.
Check that disputed or paid invoices do not receive reminders.

tasks.short: Administer approved licensing tests and preserve applicants’ responses.

steps.what: Arrange the test appointment and send joining instructions.
Check the applicant’s identity, prerequisites and agreed accommodations before admission.
Select the approved test version and prepare materials.
Explain written-test rules, supervise completion and manage interruptions.
Conduct oral or practical exercises and intervene when safety requires.
File responses, attendance and incidents against the applicant’s case.

tasks.design: Configure appointments and instructions in the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}, with approved digital written tests in the {LMS} where permitted. Store responses and structured session records in the {DOCS}; examiners retain identity checks, accommodations, live supervision and safety interventions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical supervision dominated the task, while scheduling, test versions and evidence storage were handled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling, assessment and records features can handle the administration. AI-assisted coding can shorten the work needed to connect them.
tasks.still_hard: Recognised test formats, accessibility, identity assurance, equipment safety and unreliable connectivity can restrict digital delivery.
tasks.human_edge: The examiner notices distress, unsafe behaviour and unusual circumstances, and responds fairly in real time.

ambition.what: Offer an additional evening written-test session for shift workers.

tasks.altitude: The examiner spends less time arranging sessions and filing records. The examiner can propose additional sessions, but gains no licensing decision rights.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence checklist for a regulated assessment.
reach.learn: Evidence provenance, assessment independence and the limits of delegated authority.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, approved test delivery and structured records can use existing configurable software; live practical supervision remains human.
Significant licensing decisions involving personal data require assessment against GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to a regulated testing or training provider with 200 to 2,000 staff, not a typical general finance department.
The examiner is authorised to administer the relevant test; the employer does not automatically hold licensing authority.
Time shares describe a mixed caseload; individual applicants may take only written, oral or practical components.
Administration here excludes substantive scoring, which is covered by the separate scoring task.
Digital delivery replaces paper capture prospectively; historical handwritten responses are not automatically transcribed.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Access work includes GDPR and EU AI Act applicability checks, and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which test formats and digital systems the licensing authority accepts.
Whether the organisation already has a suitable {LMS}.
Required accommodations, identity checks and retention periods.
Whether examiner work records trigger employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which approved test-delivery requirements prevent use of standard assessment features?
How much administration remains after configuring the existing assessment system?
new_work: Maintain approved test versions, appointment rules and accessibility settings.
Handle scheduling failures and incomplete response records.
Check record access and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Administer oral, written, road, or flight tests to license applicants.

tasks.short: Inspect premises for displayed permits and compliance with licensing conditions.

steps.what: Assemble the permit record, previous findings and inspection checklist.
Travel to the premises and obtain access.
Check displayed permits against the premises, activities and current permit record.
Inspect operations and equipment against licensing conditions, recording supporting evidence.
Discuss discrepancies and obtain the site representative’s explanation.
Compile the inspection report and link each finding to evidence.
Confirm findings, distinguish uncertainty and approve the inspection report.

tasks.design: Build inspection packs from approved permit data and standards in the {DOCS}, using permitted access to the {GOV_PORTAL}. Configure an offline inspection form in the {WORKFLOW} that links evidence to conditions and generates a report from recorded findings. The officer inspects the premises, hears explanations and approves the report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Permit details, field notes and photographs were separate, so officers assembled the same evidence twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Offline forms, structured evidence links and template generation are established capabilities; small integrations are cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Physical access, hidden conditions, disputed evidence and current permit data still require effort. A checklist cannot establish that every licensing condition is satisfied.
tasks.human_edge: The officer recognises unusual site conditions and distinguishes a paperwork discrepancy from a substantive breach.
tasks.altitude: Less report assembly leaves more time for difficult sites and repeat findings. The officer can recommend inspection priorities; enforcement powers remain defined by the existing mandate.

reach.task: Prioritise sites using repeat findings and unresolved exposure.
reach.learn: Risk weighting, sampling bias and uncertainty in inspection coverage.

evidence.claim: Offline inspection forms, evidence registers and template reports can reduce paperwork without replacing physical inspection.
The proposed effort reductions and build ranges are estimates; the digest supplies no directly comparable inspection case.

assumptions: The organisation operates regulated premises or provides authorised inspection services.
A company compliance officer reports findings and does not gain statutory enforcement powers through this tool.
Report generation inserts structured findings and preserves explanations verbatim; it does not interpret free text or infer breaches.
The future form captures evidence once, reducing later report assembly.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes GDPR requirements for photographs and personal data, EU AI Act applicability, and consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether inspections are internal assurance visits or formally delegated statutory inspections.
How permit validity can be checked and how often source records change.
Whether photographs and offline storage are permitted at inspected sites.
Travel time, connectivity and actual report preparation effort.
research_questions: Which licensing conditions require direct observation rather than document evidence?
Can structured findings produce an acceptable report without narrative rewriting?
new_work: Maintain inspection standards and permit-data mappings.
Resolve offline synchronisation failures and missing evidence.
Review generated reports for omissions and outdated permit references.
Maintain photograph access and retention controls.
tasks.statement: Visit establishments to verify that valid licenses or permits are displayed and that licensing standards are being upheld.

tasks.short: Score written tests and assess applicants’ practical operating ability.

steps.what: Retrieve responses and select the applicable scoring rubric.
Mark written answers and calculate the written score.
Observe practical operation and record performance against the rubric.
Assess practical competence, critical faults and incomplete evidence against the rubric.
Validate the combined assessment and sign the applicant’s rating record.

tasks.design: Configure approved objective answer keys and versioned scoring rules in the {LMS}. Capture practical observations through the {WORKFLOW}, then assemble the score, rationale and evidence links in the {DOCS}. The examiner assesses practical competence and signs the complete rating before it supports a licensing decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Straightforward marking and arithmetic were bundled with practical judgement, while scoring rubrics were managed as separate documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing assessment features can score objective answers and check completeness. Small connections can assemble the rating record without automating practical judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Critical faults, borderline competence and inconsistent examiner interpretations need professional judgement and calibration.
tasks.human_edge: The examiner judges safe, consistent operation in context and can explain why an observed action matters.

ambition.what: Run a monthly examiner calibration clinic using disputed rubric examples.

tasks.altitude: The examiner spends less time marking objective answers and assembling records. More time goes to borderline assessments and calibration; licensing decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Sample rating records for missing evidence and rubric-version errors.
reach.learn: Audit sampling, evidence sufficiency and independent review.

evidence.claim: Objective answer-key scoring and arithmetic can be configured; practical competence requires contextual assessment.
Meaningful human intervention matters when automated processing supports decisions with significant effects.
A determining score can itself fall within the scope of automated decision rules; the cited judgment concerns credit scoring.

assumptions: Written marking in this baseline uses objective answers with an approved answer key; essay or oral scoring would remain human.
Future written responses are captured digitally through the separate test-administration task.
Practical observation occurs during the administered session; it is assessment effort, not a second test session.
The rating supports a separate licensing decision and does not automatically issue or refuse a licence.
No video-based behaviour inference, emotion recognition or model-generated practical score is proposed.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes GDPR review, EU AI Act applicability, and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: The proportion of objective written questions versus answers requiring judgement.
Which rubric rules and critical faults the authority permits software to calculate.
Required examiner independence, countersignatures and appeal evidence.
Whether applicants can inspect or challenge their rating records.
research_questions: Which scoring rules are fully specified and independently testable?
How often do examiners disagree on the same practical evidence?
new_work: Validate answer keys and scoring thresholds before each approved version goes live.
Investigate disputed scores and incomplete assessment records.
Maintain rubric versions and examiner calibration examples.
Check that human sign-off remains substantive.
tasks.statement: Score tests and observe equipment operation and control to rate ability of applicants.

tasks.short: Prepare and send approved licensing decision notices with accurate appeal instructions.

steps.what: Retrieve the approved licensing decision, reasons and recipient details.
Check the applicable appeal route, service rules and deadline.
Draft the decision notice using the approved wording and case reasons.
Review the recipient, decision, reasons and appeal instructions; approve release.
Send the approved notice through the required channel and retain dispatch evidence.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator combines approved decisions, unchanged case reasons and versioned notice clauses from the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} checks required fields and routes the exact notice for signatory approval. It releases only that approved version through the permitted {EMAIL} channel and stores dispatch evidence in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decisions, appeal clauses and contact details were copied between documents and mailboxes, with no reliable link between approval and dispatch.
tasks.enabler_now: Template generation, rule tables and approval workflows are established. AI-assisted coding can make the connecting work cheaper without generating legal reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual decisions, contested reasons and service rules need specialist review. Dispatch evidence does not necessarily prove legally effective service.
tasks.human_edge: The signatory checks that the notice expresses the actual decision fairly and gives the recipient a usable route to challenge it.

ambition.what: Provide a same-day appeal-route clarification service after notice dispatch.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time copying text and chasing approvals, and more time resolving unclear notices. Dispatch can follow standing rules, while legal interpretation and release approval remain with the authorised roles.

reach.task: Reconcile approved notices with dispatch records.
reach.learn: Approval evidence, segregation of duties and exception sampling.

evidence.claim: Approved clauses, structured case fields and unchanged reasons can generate notices without a language model.
The digest documents regulatory registration tracking and submission publishing, an adjacent capability rather than evidence for licensing correspondence.
The digest documents a report containing nonexistent sources, supporting source checks if generated legal prose is later considered.

assumptions: The licensing decision and substantive reasons have already been approved; this task communicates them.
The baseline uses a small set of approved templates and email service where legally permitted.
The generator inserts reasons unchanged and does not infer legal grounds or rewrite disputed reasoning.
Appeal rules are versioned by jurisdiction, decision type and effective date; unmatched cases stop for specialist handling.
Dispatch requires approval tied to the exact document and recipient; any change invalidates that approval.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes GDPR, EU AI Act applicability, and consultation under national rules where employee work records are affected.
unknowns: Who holds authority to approve release and who owns legal template updates.
Which delivery channels satisfy applicable national rules.
Whether deadlines run from decision, dispatch, receipt or another event.
How many decisions require bespoke explanations or translated notices.
Whether existing records expose stable case identifiers and approval status.
research_questions: What proportion of notices can use approved clauses without rewriting case reasons?
Which service events and deadline calculations can be represented as explicit rules?
new_work: Maintain notice clauses, appeal rules and effective dates.
Review unmatched jurisdictions and exceptional service requirements.
Resolve failed delivery and incorrect recipient details.
Audit that dispatched documents match their approved versions.
tasks.statement: Prepare correspondence to inform concerned parties of licensing decisions or appeals processes.

tasks.short: Identify possible compliance breaches and decide which need investigation.

steps.what: Collect complaints, control exceptions and relevant transaction records.
Read case documents against relevant obligations and policies.

loop.input: Case evidence and approved, versioned obligations and policies.
loop.output: Possible issues with source passages, contradictions and missing evidence.
loop.check: Verify source references and versions; the officer checks material claims before investigation decisions.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction per case; unresolved conflicts return to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative complaints and case documents describe possible breaches in varied language.

steps.what: Check dates, thresholds and transaction patterns in exported records.
Decide whether the evidence warrants follow-up, investigation or closure.
Record the decision and assign follow-up with a deadline.

tasks.design: A connector on the {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers permitted evidence from the {ERP}, {HELPDESK} and {WORKFLOW}, then runs approved control rules. A bounded reading loop compares narrative evidence with versioned obligations in the {DOCS}; the compliance officer decides the disposition before the {WORKFLOW} assigns follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits across systems, and narrative allegations rarely fit fixed rules. Bespoke connectors and evidence tracing were costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can reduce connector and rule-engine development effort. Bounded document reading can produce source-linked drafts; legal judgement remains necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Contradictory evidence, privilege, sensitive allegations and uncertain legal applicability. Access controls and false-negative testing remain substantial work.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh credibility, context and proportionality, and distinguish a weak signal from a serious breach.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting files to reviewing evidence and choosing investigation priorities. With delegated authority, the officer can redirect investigation capacity across controls.

reach.task: Triage suspicious payment patterns alongside compliance allegations.
reach.learn: Evidence preservation, fraud indicators and the limits of pattern-based suspicion.

reach.task: Assess the financial exposure of recurring control exceptions.
reach.learn: Exposure estimation and risk appetite thresholds.

evidence.claim: Structured thresholds and deadlines support deterministic checks; narrative allegations still require judgement.
Shift Technology documents fraud screening in insurance; this supports screening feasibility, not general compliance accuracy.
GDPR Article 22 requires a separate assessment when automation makes legally or similarly significant decisions about people.
Dutch requirements include a mandatory DPIA list covering specified fraud-prevention and monitoring processing; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: A typical mid-size company has digital case records and some spreadsheet-based checks.
Flags inform investigation decisions and do not automatically impose sanctions.
The judgement prior is retained; record gathering and explicit checks are more automatable.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one case queue and a limited connector set, not sourced performance claims.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; purpose and deployment determine relevant duties. Employee consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Available case systems, interfaces and evidence permissions.
Applicable obligations, sector rules and approved control thresholds.
Whether cases involve employees, customers or legally significant decisions.
Investigation authority, escalation thresholds and retention requirements.
Required consultation, DPIA and access-approval lead times.
research_questions: Which existing configurations can replace spreadsheet checks?
How well does source-linked triage perform on independently labelled historic cases?
Which exceptions reveal missing data rather than possible non-compliance?
new_work: Review narrative issue drafts and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain versioned control rules and obligation mappings.
Monitor missed issues and excessive flags using sampled cases.
Maintain connectors, permissions and evidence retention.
tasks.statement: Identify compliance issues that require follow-up or investigation.

tasks.short: Track regulatory and industry developments and assess their relevance.

steps.what: Scan subscribed alerts and newsletters for new developments.
Read official notices, proposals and industry guidance.

loop.input: Retrieved source documents from the approved source register.
loop.output: Source-linked changes, proposal status, affected activities and stated effective dates.
loop.check: Validate every reference and quoted date against retrieved text; inspect material changes in the source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unreadable or conflicting sources enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notices describe changes in prose and use inconsistent document structures.

steps.what: Record changes, remove duplicates and note expected dates.
Assess applicability, uncertainty and whether a policy review is needed.
Share relevant extracts and review recommendations with affected teams.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} collects subscribed alerts and maintains a deduplicated change register, with source-linked summaries stored in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares the reading brief, and the compliance officer records applicability decisions before approved findings appear in the {BI} and trigger targeted notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source formats and update schedules vary. Collecting alerts was feasible, but useful summaries and applicability checks required sustained reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing subscriptions and scheduled retrieval handle collection. Bounded extraction and faster connector development reduce preparation effort without resolving legal uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing proposals from binding requirements, finding amendments and judging effects on specific activities. Restricted sources and incomplete coverage remain problems.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which developments matter to the business and when uncertain guidance warrants specialist advice.

ambition.what: Monthly regulatory horizon clinic for finance process owners

tasks.altitude: The week includes less alert scanning and more focused reading and discussion with process owners. No new decision rights arise automatically; the officer can recommend earlier reviews.

reach.task: Translate upcoming regulatory changes into budget and resource implications.
reach.learn: Budget cycles, implementation costs and dependencies between finance processes.

reach.task: Assess which regulatory developments require filing-process changes.
reach.learn: Filing calendars, tax-specific applicability and evidence requirements.

evidence.claim: Subscriptions, duplicate detection and source registers can automate collection without deciding legal applicability.
Veeva RIM tracks registrations and submissions in a regulated sector; it does not establish generic horizon-scanning capability.
A documented report failure involving nonexistent sources supports checking generated references against retrieved originals.

assumptions: The source set includes public official material and authorised subscriptions.
The gathering prior is retained, but professional learning and applicability assessment remain human work.
Unreviewed summaries carry draft status and do not amend the obligation register.
Build ranges are planning estimates for a limited source set.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Internal confidential context is excluded from public-source retrieval.
unknowns: Relevant jurisdictions, sectors, business activities and source subscriptions.
Source licensing and permitted retrieval methods.
Who can approve obligation-register changes.
Whether internal business context may enter the reading service.
Required source languages and update cadence.
research_questions: Which official sources offer feeds or stable retrieval interfaces?
How often are material developments missed by the existing source set?
Can date and legal-status extraction distinguish proposals, adoption and commencement reliably?
new_work: Maintain the source register and repair failed retrievals.
Check material summaries against original text.
Resolve duplicate, amended and conflicting notices.
Review source coverage and retire low-value alerts.
tasks.statement: Keep informed regarding pending industry changes, trends, or best practices.

tasks.short: Help auditors obtain evidence, understand controls and resolve compliance review questions.

steps.what: Clarify audit requests, scope, deadlines and permitted disclosures.
Request missing evidence from control owners and track responses.
Retrieve transaction records and control results for requested periods.
Check evidence completeness and prepare explanations with an evidence index.

loop.input: Agreed requests and authorised evidence with identifiers and reporting periods.
loop.output: Draft explanations linked to an evidence index, with explicit gaps and limitations.
loop.check: Code checks identifiers, periods and totals; the officer verifies each material explanation.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per request; unsupported answers remain marked as gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: Auditors ask varied narrative questions that require explanations across several documents.

steps.what: Approve disclosure and release the evidence package to the auditor.
Explain control operation, discuss gaps and agree follow-up.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} tracks agreed requests and gathers authorised evidence through connectors to the {ERP} and {DOCS}. A deterministic package builder creates the index, while a bounded loop drafts source-linked explanations; the compliance officer approves each release and handles auditor discussions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive in different formats, evidence ownership is scattered, and disclosure needs judgement. Standard trackers helped coordination but did not assemble defensible answers.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured request workflows and reusable extraction code handle much of the preparation. Bounded drafting can join evidence into explanations with references for review.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence quality, privilege, disclosure boundaries and contested findings. Explaining how controls work in practice still requires knowledgeable people.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust with auditors, acknowledge weaknesses candidly and challenge conclusions using defensible evidence.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing attachments to resolving evidence gaps and preparing control owners for review. The officer gains no automatic authority over audit findings or remediation budgets.

reach.task: Reconcile audit extracts to financial control totals.
reach.learn: Ledger reconciliation, period cut-offs and accounting evidence.

reach.task: Assess whether evidence demonstrates control operation.
reach.learn: Sampling, audit assertions and independence boundaries.

evidence.claim: Request tracking, evidence indexing and period-based extraction support deterministic preparation.
A documented generated-report failure supports verifying citations before releasing audit explanations.
DNB reported documentation and monitoring weaknesses in insurer AI use; that evidence is sector-specific.

assumptions: The compliance officer supports audits rather than independently determining the auditor's findings.
Audits commonly combine calls, mailbox coordination, system extracts and document packages.
The human-task prior applies to scope and explanation; preparation has substantial automation potential.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one audit process and a limited evidence set.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Employee-related evidence and consultation require assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Auditor access arrangements and permitted disclosure channels.
Evidence locations, owners, retention and privilege restrictions.
Who has authority to release each evidence category.
Whether extraction can reproduce historical records and control totals.
Required employee consultation and access approvals.
research_questions: Which evidence requests recur enough to support fixed extraction templates?
Can packages preserve reproducible snapshots and source versions?
Which explanations require interviews because documentary evidence is insufficient?
new_work: Review draft explanations and evidence gaps.
Approve releases and check disclosure permissions.
Maintain extraction templates and evidence-owner mappings.
Test package completeness and manage access expiry.
tasks.statement: Provide assistance to internal or external auditors in compliance reviews.

tasks.short: Verify that policies are documented, operating and communicated to affected people.

steps.what: Compare applicable obligations with the policy register and document versions.

loop.input: Approved obligations, policy text, document versions and prior mappings.
loop.output: Suggested coverage links with quoted passages and possible gaps.
loop.check: Validate document versions and references; the officer confirms coverage before accepting mappings.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair per policy; ambiguous obligations remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Policies express obligations in different wording, and a keyword match cannot establish coverage.

steps.what: Ask policy owners for implementation evidence and missing documentation.
Inspect control records for evidence that procedures operate.
Check publication, acknowledgements and required training completion.
Resolve conflicting evidence with policy owners and decide whether gaps remain.
Record assurance status and assign corrective actions with deadlines.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} holds obligation, policy and control links, requests evidence and tracks corrective actions. Connectors check version and completion records from the {DOCS}, {ERP}, {LMS} and {HCM}; a bounded reading loop suggests policy coverage, while the compliance officer signs assurance decisions before status reaches the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy documents, operating evidence and communication records use different identifiers and owners. Document existence was easier to verify than effective implementation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured records and reminders handle ownership and deadlines. Faster integration development and bounded text comparison reduce reconciliation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Proving that procedures work, interpreting partial coverage and reaching contractors or staff outside standard records. Completion data does not establish understanding.
tasks.human_edge: Test whether a policy changes real behaviour and challenge reassuring paperwork that lacks operating evidence.

ambition.what: Monthly prioritisation of policy implementation gaps

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting acknowledgements to testing weak controls and discussing practical fixes. With delegated authority, the officer can set corrective-action priorities; policy approval remains with its authorised owner.

reach.task: Test control effectiveness using targeted evidence samples.
reach.learn: Sampling design and the difference between control design and operating effectiveness.

reach.task: Build reliable policy coverage and remediation reporting.
reach.learn: Data lineage, denominator definitions and access-controlled reporting.

evidence.claim: Version checks, owner reminders and completion reconciliation support deterministic automation; effective implementation still needs evidence assessment.
Dutch works-council law includes consent rights for specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.
Employee evaluation can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories; administrative completion tracking alone does not establish that classification.
DNB documented weaknesses in insurer AI documentation and monitoring, supporting checks beyond the existence of policy documents.

assumptions: Policies have identifiable owners and approved versions, although cross-system mappings may be incomplete.
The document-heavy prior is retained; the decomposition gives more time to operating-evidence checks than document formatting.
Completion checks support assurance and do not score employee performance.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one policy family and a limited system set.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Consultation, monitoring and employment requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Policy ownership, approved obligation mappings and evidence standards.
Interfaces and identifiers shared by employee, training and policy records.
Whether contractors and other affected groups appear in scope records.
Whether use of individual completion records constitutes employee monitoring.
Required consultation, privacy assessment and access-approval times.
Authority to accept residual gaps and assign remediation.
research_questions: Which existing workflow and learning configurations already provide the required records?
Which controls can be tested from system evidence, and which require observation or interviews?
How accurately do proposed coverage links distinguish partial coverage from full coverage?
new_work: Review suggested obligation-to-policy mappings.
Investigate missing evidence and conflicting completion records.
Maintain policy ownership, scope mappings and test definitions.
Sample operating controls and review access to employee-level records.
Track overdue remediation and verify closure evidence.
tasks.statement: Verify that all firm and regulatory policies and procedures have been documented, implemented, and communicated.

role_batches.altitude: The compliance officer moves from document assembly and status chasing toward evidence assessment, practical advice and earlier remediation discussions. Legal, licensing, sanction and budget authority remain within existing delegations.
reach: Financial risk assessment of overdue remedies.
Financial planning for permit dependencies and remediation.
Reliable compliance metrics with the business intelligence analyst.
skills_to_grow: Translate approved obligations into testable checks.
Assess evidence provenance and contradictory records.
Review source-linked extraction and drafting.
Explain uncertainty and proportionate remedies.
Define metrics and reconcile case data with financial records.
Assess GDPR, EU AI Act and applicable national consultation requirements.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a permit-readiness preflight service and bring current evidence to weekly remediation funding decisions, while retaining human assessment of disputed facts and legal consequences.

role_batches.altitude: The compliance officer spends more time interpreting obligations, conducting interviews and resolving contested evidence. Preparation, record updates and routine fee administration shrink, while existing legal and financial approval rights remain explicit.
reach: Accountants and auditors: prepare traceable evidence packs and test control failures.
Financial risk specialists: prioritise incidents using exposure and reporting deadlines.
Financial examiners: assess evidence sufficiency for authorisation decisions.
Billing and posting clerks: maintain reliable fee and payment records.
skills_to_grow: Translate obligations into versioned checks with explicit exceptions.
Verify source-linked model outputs and identify unsupported conclusions.
Conduct fair interviews and preserve evidence attribution.
Understand record identifiers, reconciliation and approval controls.
Assess GDPR and EU AI Act applicability and relevant national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A compliance evidence service that gives applicants and internal teams early completeness checks, while officers focus on difficult facts, defensible decisions and timely regulatory reporting.

role_batches.altitude: The compliance officer retains field judgement, practical assessment and accountable release decisions. The week shifts away from assembling packs, marking objective answers and copying notices toward disputed evidence, examiner calibration and clear explanations; statutory powers do not change.
reach: Financial risk specialist: use repeat findings to recommend inspection priorities.
Accountant and auditor: sample assessment evidence and reconcile approvals with dispatch.
Financial examiner: prepare defensible evidence checklists for regulated assessments.
skills_to_grow: Translate approved standards into testable rules and versioned templates.
Design evidence records that support review and appeals.
Configure workflows, access controls and exception queues.
Calibrate practical judgement across examiners.
Assess GDPR, EU AI Act and applicable national-rule requirements for the actual use.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Use the released administrative capacity to run examiner calibration clinics, review repeat-breach inspection priorities weekly and provide prompt appeal-route clarification, within the organisation’s existing mandate.

role_batches.altitude: The compliance officer spends more of the week interpreting evidence, discussing weak controls and prioritising follow-up. New investigation or remediation rights require explicit delegation; automation alone grants none.
reach: Support fraud analysts with source-linked case triage.
Help accountants produce reproducible audit evidence.
Work with financial managers on regulatory implementation costs.
Partner with internal auditors on control effectiveness testing.
Help business intelligence analysts define trustworthy assurance measures.

Assess evidence quality, lineage and missing-data risks.
Review source-linked model drafts and measure errors using independent samples.
Design proportionate access, retention and disclosure controls.
Use financial materiality and risk appetite to prioritise investigations.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
